item.title: Secretary of State Rubio’s Call with UK Foreign Secretary Miliband
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Secretary of State Rubio’s Call with UK Foreign Secretary Miliband

Readout

October 12, 2026

The following is attributable to Spokesman Tommy Pigott:

 Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke today with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband.  They reiterated their shared commitment to safeguarding transit in the Strait of Hormuz and the importance of holding Iran to account for its actions and of continued collaboration to secure U.S. assets in the United Kingdom.  Secretary Rubio reaffirmed the value of our close partnership to stabilize global energy markets while also bringing the Russia-Ukraine conflict to an end through a negotiated settlement.

item.title: Second U.S.-Japan Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP) Dialogue
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Second U.S.-Japan Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP) Dialogue

Media Note

October 12, 2026

Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs Allison Hooker and Japanese Senior Deputy Minister for Foreign Affairs Namazu Hiroyuki held the second U.S.-Japan Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP) Dialogue on October 12 in Tokyo.  The dialogue marked the 10th anniversary of the Free and Open Indo-Pacific vision.  The two sides noted continued close alignment on U.S. priorities and Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae’s updated Free and Open Indo-Pacific.  They committed to turning that shared vision into concrete results for the American and Japanese people and for the Indo-Pacific region.  Under Secretary Hooker and Senior Deputy Minister Namazu discussed how to align their foreign assistance behind strategic infrastructure in priority countries, including the Luzon Economic Corridor in the Philippines and the Japan-U.S. Mekong Power Partnership (JUMPP).  They also agreed to coordinate security assistance more closely, especially for maritime security and maritime domain awareness in Southeast Asia and the Pacific Islands.

The two sides reviewed progress on economic security, including critical minerals supply chains, deep-sea mineral development, digital connectivity, and energy security.  On regional security, they discussed working more closely with allies and partners in the region, and they welcomed Japan’s growing cooperation with NATO.  They noted progress in U.S.-Japan defense industrial cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to the complete denuclearization of the DPRK and the immediate resolution of the abductions issue.

item.title: Joint Statement on the United Kingdom’s Attribution of Iran’s Involvement in Attempted Terrorist Attack at RAF Fairford
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Joint Statement on the United Kingdom’s Attribution of Iran’s Involvement in Attempted Terrorist Attack at RAF Fairford

Media Note

October 12, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America, the United Kingdom, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, and Sweden.

Begin Text.

The United States of America, the United Kingdom, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, and Sweden condemn in the strongest terms Iran’s use of violent attacks, including the acts of lethal plotting, arson, sabotage, cyber-attacks, and other hybrid activities against us and our partners.

We recognize the United Kingdom’s attribution of Iran’s involvement in the incident at RAF Fairford on 27 September.  The UK has also concluded this event demonstrates the IRGC’s continued willingness to project hostile activity beyond its borders through covert networks and proxy actors.

This comes soon after the recent campaign of attacks across Europe targeting Jewish communities, Iranian journalists, and U.S. interests, claimed by Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (HAYI).

Any attempt by Iran to threaten, silence, intimidate, harass, harm, or coerce people on our territories through proxies or any other means is unacceptable.  Anyone who conducts hostile activities on behalf of Iran, or any other state, should know that we will take action to identify, investigate, disrupt, and prosecute these acts.  Iran should be in no doubt that we are united and remain committed to safeguarding our sovereignty and strengthening our international coordination, bolstering our national resilience, protecting our communities, and ensuring that those responsible are held to account.

End Text.

item.title: Spain National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Spain National Day

Press Statement

October 12, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I extend congratulations to Spain and its citizens today on La Fiesta Nacional de España.

As the United States celebrates its 250th anniversary this year, we recognize the support Spain provided during our fight for freedom in the American Revolution along with the deepening economic ties and cultural values we share today. To advance priorities essential to the security and prosperity of both our nations, the United States will continue to urge Spain to take meaningful steps to retain strong and secure borders, combat mass migration, and increase investment in the defense capabilities needed to strengthen European security.

On this special day, I wish the Spanish people a joyous celebration and a prosperous year ahead.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Equatorial Guinea National Day

Press Statement

October 12, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I extend our warm congratulations to the people of Equatorial Guinea in honor of the 58th anniversary of your independence on October 12.

The United States values our growing partnership with Equatorial Guinea, particularly the expanding commercial ties between our two countries, including recent agreements between Equatoguinean and U.S. energy companies. We look forward to building on this momentum to unlock further opportunities for U.S. private sector investment and mutual economic growth.

In the coming year, we look forward to deepening our commercial, security, and diplomatic ties, and we extend our heartfelt wishes for peace and prosperity for the people of Equatorial Guinea.

item.title: The United States Mobilizes Immediate Response to the Panama Earthquakes
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

The United States Mobilizes Immediate Response to the Panama Earthquakes

Fact Sheet

October 10, 2026

The Trump Administration has mobilized an immediate response to the 7.7 magnitude earthquake that struck Panama on October 9. The State Department deployed Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) technical teams to conduct expert structural assessments of damage and potential immediate assistance needs at the request of the Panamanian government.  Department of War teams are assisting with the response through the U.S.-Panama Bilateral Security Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding (MOU).  Ambassador Kevin Cabrera and the State Department continue to liaise with President José Raúl Mulino and the Panamanian government as they assess the damage.

Disaster Assistance Response Team and Search and Rescue Experts Mobilized

The State Department mobilized a Disaster Assistance Response Team (DART) to coordinate and support the emergency response, including two USAR technical teams, with 20 people total, bringing a range of assessment, search, and rescue expertise. These USAR team members arrived in Panama within 24 hours of the earthquake.  The USAR technical teams will conduct aerial and on-the-ground assessments and provide additional technical assistance in coordination with local authorities. The Department also authorized Panama’s Air and Naval Service to use two INL-supported helicopters for earthquake relief.  

Humanitarian Assistance

The Department has committed to provide $5 million in assistance to support trusted on the ground implementers conducting relief efforts.

SOUTHCOM Logistical Support

Demonstrating the value of ongoing security cooperation efforts between Panama and the United States, the Department of War is supporting aerial damage assessments in the Azuero peninsula and Cocle, including joint assessments with the DART, Embassy staff, and Panamanian officials. The State Department is coordinating with SOUTHCOM to determine if additional logistical support will be required.

Supporting Americans in Panama

The Trump Administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of Americans.  The Department of State is providing consular assistance to U.S. citizens in the affected area and their families.  We are not aware of any American casualties at this time.  Our Consular Affairs hotline is available 24/7 for affected Americans in need of support at +1-202-501-4444 from abroad and +1-888-407-4747 from the U.S. and Canada.  We strongly encourage Americans in the affected areas to monitor local news, follow the emergency instructions provided by local authorities, and enroll in STEP.state.gov to receive important emergency information.

item.title: Secretary Rubio’s Call with Japanese Foreign Minister Motegi
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Secretary Rubio’s Call with Japanese Foreign Minister Motegi

Readout

October 10, 2026

Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke today with Japanese Foreign Minister Motegi Toshimitsu. The Secretary and Foreign Minister Motegi reaffirmed the strength of the U.S.-Japan Alliance, which is the cornerstone of peace, security, and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific and beyond. Secretary Rubio expressed sincere condolences over the death of a Japanese national in Okinawa, as well as the United States’ determination to communicate and fully cooperate with the Government of Japan and local authorities as they conduct an investigation. The Secretary also raised the necessity of U.S. sanctions on the International Criminal Court as a result of the Court’s rogue actions that threaten American sovereignty. He and Foreign Minister Motegi committed to continued close coordination ahead of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta.

item.title: Reconciliation Talks Deliver Concrete Progress for Venezuela’s Democratic Transition
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Reconciliation Talks Deliver Concrete Progress for Venezuela’s Democratic Transition

Fact Sheet

October 9, 2026

Political reconciliation talks between the interim Venezuelan government and 2015 National Assembly representatives are producing tangible reforms in civil liberties and political rights, laying the groundwork for credible elections and a democratic transition.  Two rounds of talks have already taken place, producing significant results:  a wholesale reform and reconstruction of an independent Venezuelan Supreme Court, the restoration of access to more than 70 previously blocked internet domains, and the reform of a key repressive law.  The interim government has also released more than 1,000 political prisoners and announced the release of nearly 200 more.   

The talks bring together representatives of Venezuela’s 2015 National Assembly, led by its President Dinorah Figuera, and representatives of the interim government, led by current National Assembly President Jorge Rodríguez.  The 2015 National Assembly was Venezuela’s last democratically elected legislative body recognized by all Venezuelan political parties and by the international community.   

The delegations held two rounds of talks in Caracas in August and September, with another round scheduled to begin October 14.  The parties have decided to remain in session to maintain the momentum they have achieved.  

The United States supports this Venezuelan-led process to create the conditions for a peaceful democratic transition, which is only possible because of President Trump’s bold leadership. Early accomplishments include the following: 

Rebuilding an Independent Supreme Court:

  • Following the talks, the 2026 National Assembly published a law reforming the Supreme Court selection process, with 32 new judges to be selected by December.  The Supreme Court will adjudicate any challenges to Venezuela’s future election results, underscoring the importance of a credible selection process. 
  • The talks led to the creation of a seven-member Credentials Council, an unprecedented all-judge body that will screen candidates and send only qualified jurists to the Judicial Nominations Committee.  Importantly, the 2015 National Assembly chose a majority of the Council. 
  • The Judicial Nominations Committee, made up of 11 current National Assembly members and 12 civil society members, will choose the 32 nominees from the Credentials Council’s approved list. 
  • This selection process increases transparency and enshrines protections to ensure the new judges will be qualified and not tied to the Maduro regime. 

Expanding Freedom of Expression:

  • The interim government has restored or partially restored access to more than 70 previously blocked internet domains, including El Tiempo, EFE, Revista Semana, El Pitazo, Efecto Cucuyo, among others. 

Reforming Repressive Laws:

  • The National Assembly established a commission to reform and decriminalize penalties contained in the repressive 2017 Law Against Hatred, which was notorious for its use by the Maduro regime to jail opposition leaders and those who spoke out against the regime. 
  • The law established penalties of up to 20 years in prison for the “promotion or incitement of hatred, discrimination, or violence,” although in practice it was used to punish criticism of the regime.   

Releasing Political Prisoners: 

  • The interim government has released over 1,000 political prisoners since Operation Absolute Resolve.  Since the political reconciliation talks began in August, the interim government has announced the release of an additional 177 political prisoners, an important step toward restoring fundamental political freedoms.   
  • Prominent political prisoners released since January 3 include Juan Pablo Guanipa, advisor to Maria Corina Machado and former First Vice President of the National Assembly; Freddy Superlano, ex-gubernatorial candidate and former National Assembly member; and Enrique Márquez, ex-presidential candidate and former Vice President of the National Electoral Council. 
  • Exiled opposition figures Claudia Macero and Omar González Moreno, who fled the threat of detention due to political motivated charges, have also returned to Venezuela.  

What Comes Next  

  • The third round of reconciliation talks is scheduled to begin October 14.  The delegations will focus on finalizing the Supreme Court selection process and providing individuals and political parties participation guarantees necessary for credible elections.   
  • Future rounds of dialogue will address reform of the National Electoral Council, repealing remaining repressive laws, and opening political space so all political parties and leaders can return and participate in political life.   
  • We welcome the joint efforts with Venezuela’s interim government to recover the gold in the United Kingdom. 

The Trump Administration will continue to support this Venezuelan-led process as it moves from dialogue to durable democratic institutions. 

For media inquiries, please contact the Office of the Spokesman.

item.title: Secretary Rubio’s Meeting with Venezuela’s 2015 National Assembly President Dinorah Figuera
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Secretary Rubio’s Meeting with Venezuela’s 2015 National Assembly President Dinorah Figuera

Readout

October 9, 2026

Secretary of State Marco Rubio met today in Washington with Venezuela’s 2015 National Assembly President Dinorah Figuera. 

The Secretary commended Figuera’s courageous leadership in advancing political reconciliation following Operation Absolute Resolve and welcomed the tangible progress achieved during the first two rounds of talks with the interim authorities.  He highlighted this year’s steps toward establishing an independent Supreme Court of Justice, the release of over 1,200 political prisoners, the recently restored access to blocked media websites, and efforts to reform the Law Against Hatred as important milestones toward restoring fundamental freedoms for the Venezuelan people. 

Looking ahead to the next round of talks beginning October 14, the Secretary urged continued progress on political freedoms and electoral reform, which would lay the groundwork for free, fair, and credible elections in Venezuela.  Both reaffirmed their commitment to building on the momentum of the talks and translating this historic opportunity into lasting democratic change for the Venezuelan people.
